mainTopic: The end of the brothers' letter, who will rise at תחיית המתים, and the future abundance of ארץ ישראל
overview: This amud finishes the letter that רבה's brothers sent him from ארץ ישראל. The letter ends with a saying about support and a report that three sages rule like רבי יהודה: a female mule may mate only with another mule. רבי אלעזר then says that עמי הארץ will not come alive at תחיית המתים. רבי יוחנן objects, and רבי אלעזר answers that anyone who supports תלמידי חכמים counts as cleaving to the שכינה and so has a share in that life. Next, רבי חייא בר יוסף and a series of ברייתות describe the future: צדיקים rising in ירושלים fully dressed, giant wheat, and huge grapes. רב דימי reads יעקב's ברכה to יהודה as a picture of the land's amazing wine, and he also gives the פסוק's plain meaning, which supports רבי יוחנן's teaching about the value of a smile. The amud ends with eyewitness stories of the land's rich produce and its milk and honey, and רבה בר בר חנה's report continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Standing with support is better than sitting without it
steps.stepSummary: The brothers finish a saying: sitting without something to lean on is worse than standing with something to lean on.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Sitting] that has no support: standing that has support is more comfortable than it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a saying from the brothers' letter to רבה. The saying started just before this section. It means that a lower position with real support is better than a higher position with nothing to lean on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is about support, not about how high the position is. Standing with something to lean on is better than sitting with nothing. The brothers use this saying in their letter to persuade רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: More comfortable than it, better than it

phrases.english: [Sitting] that has no support,

phrases.aramaic: עֲמִידָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ סְמִיכָה נוֹחָה הֵימֶנָּה.
phrases.english: standing that has support is more comfortable than it.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲמִידָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ סְמִיכָה נוֹחָה הֵימֶנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a saying from the brothers' letter, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Standing with support is better than sitting without support.

steps.title: Three sages agree: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה about mules
steps.stepSummary: The brothers report that יצחק, שמעון and אושעיא all said the same thing: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה regarding פרדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so they said: יצחק, שמעון and אושעיא all said one thing: the הלכה is like רבי יהודה regarding mules.
steps.whatsHappening: The letter goes on to report a הלכה. Three sages all agree that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה's view about פרדות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the letter only names רבי יהודה's view without saying what it is. The next step quotes the ברייתא that spells it out. The fact that three separate sages agree makes the ruling stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the view of...

phrases.english: And so they said:
Yitzchak, Shimon and Oshaya
said one and the same thing:
the halacha is like Rabbi Yehuda regarding mules.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the brothers' letter with a new report about a הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יהודה regarding פרדות.

steps.title: What רבי יהודה ruled: a mule may mate only with its own kind
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: a female mule in heat may not be mated with a horse or a donkey, only with another mule.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי יהודה says: a female mule in heat may not be mated with a horse or a donkey, only with her own kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that shows what רבי יהודה's view actually is. This explains the ruling in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mule comes from a horse and a donkey, but רבי יהודה treats it as its own species. So mating it with a horse or a donkey counts as mixing species (כלאים). Only another mule counts as 'her kind'.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that, by this ruling, a mule counts as a separate species for the laws of כלאים.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A female mule in heat,
one may not mate with her
neither a horse nor a donkey,
only her own kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source that spells out the view of רבי יהודה mentioned in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A female mule may be mated only with another mule, not with a horse or a donkey.

steps.title: Who the three sages are
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק identifies the three sages: יצחק is רבי יצחק נפחא, שמעון is רבי שמעון בן פזי (some say ריש לקיש), and אושעיא is רבי אושעיא בריבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: יצחק is רבי יצחק נפחא; שמעון is רבי שמעון בן פזי, and some say ריש לקיש; אושעיא is רבי אושעיא בריבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The letter gave only first names, so רב נחמן בר יצחק explains exactly which sages it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many sages shared these first names, so the identification matters. There are two versions about who שמעון is. These are well-known sages of ארץ ישראל, which gives the ruling more weight.

keyTerms.meaning: The blacksmith, a nickname of רבי יצחק
The distinguished one, a title of honor

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Yitzchak is Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha;

phrases.aramaic: שִׁמְעוֹן — זֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי,
phrases.english: Shimon is Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi;
and some say: Reish Lakish;
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש's real name was also שמעון (רבי שמעון בן לקיש), so he fits the name too.

phrases.english: Oshaya is Rabbi Oshaya the Distinguished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the names given in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יצחק = רבי יצחק נפחא; שמעון = רבי שמעון בן פזי (or ריש לקיש); אושעיא = רבי אושעיא בריבי.
steps.whatToRemember: The letter's ruling on פרדות comes from three major sages of ארץ ישראל, and the ruling follows רבי יהודה: a mule mates only with a mule.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the unlearned will not come back to life
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that עמי הארץ will not live at תחיית המתים, based on the פסוק 'The dead live not'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: The unlearned people will not live, as it says: 'The dead live not' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רבי אלעזר makes a strong statement that עמי הארץ will not come back to life, and he brings a פסוק as his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'the dead' in the פסוק as people who were already 'dead' in their lifetime because they had no Torah. Such people 'will not live', meaning they will not rise at תחיית המתים.

keyTerms.meaning: Unlearned people, those without Torah knowledge

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a ruling that most people won't come back to life. The ברייתא in the next step limits it to someone who weakens himself from Torah.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
The unlearned people will not live,
as it is said: 'The dead live not' and so on.
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 26:14

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר עַמֵּי הָאֲרָצוֹת אֵינָן חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the brothers' letter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עמי הארץ will not come alive at תחיית המתים.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports him: the verse is about one who weakens himself from Torah
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same idea. One might think 'The dead live not' means nobody will rise, so the end of the פסוק, 'רפאים will not rise', shows it means only someone who weakens himself from Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught: 'The dead live not.' One might think this applies to everyone. So the verse says: 'The shades (רפאים) rise not.' The verse is speaking of one who weakens (מרפה) himself from words of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי אלעזר. The ברייתא also makes clear exactly whom the פסוק means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the second half of the פסוק, we might think no dead person will ever rise. The word רפאים is read as connected to מרפה, 'weakens', so the פסוק means only a person who let go of Torah. That matches רבי אלעזר's claim about עמי הארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (a ברייתא supports it)

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'The dead live not' does not deny תחיית המתים in general. It refers only to someone who weakens himself from Torah.
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps the belief in תחיית המתים in place, while teaching how serious it is to neglect Torah.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
'The dead live not.'
One might think this means everyone,
so the verse says: 'The shades rise not.'
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, ישעיהו 26:14. רפאים sounds like מרפה, 'weakens', and the ברייתא builds on that.

phrases.english: about one who weakens himself from words of Torah
the verse is speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אלעזר's statement in step 5 and limits whom it covers.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's claim that עמי הארץ will not live again.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ישעיהו 26:14, connecting רפאים to מרפה, 'one who weakens himself from Torah'.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן objects: that פסוק is about idol worshippers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells רבי אלעזר that ה׳ is not pleased with his statement about עמי הארץ. He says the פסוק 'the dead live not' is really about someone who gives himself over to עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Their Master is not happy that you say this about them. That פסוק was written about someone who weakens himself to idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes back on רבי אלעזר's harsh claim that עמי הארץ will not rise at תחיית המתים. He offers a different reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that supported רבי אלעזר read 'רפאים' as 'מרפה', someone who weakens himself from Torah. רבי יוחנן keeps the same word but says it means weakening oneself to עבודה זרה. That limits the punishment to idol worshippers, not ordinary unlearned Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not pleasing / not acceptable

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי אלעזר, who made the statement in Step 5.

phrases.english: It is not pleasing to their Master
that you say this about them;
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the עמי הארץ.

phrases.english: that verse, about one who weakens himself
to idol worship, is where it is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָא נִיחָא לְמָרַיְיהוּ דְּאָמְרַתְּ לְהוּ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק used in Steps 5 and 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that עמי הארץ will not live at תחיית המתים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק can be read as being about idol worshippers, so there is no source to exclude ordinary unlearned Jews. Saying so also displeases ה׳.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר brings a different פסוק about the light of Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that he learns his idea from a different פסוק: 'For Your dew is a dew of lights'. Only someone who uses the light of Torah will be revived by it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I learn it from another פסוק. It says, 'For Your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth shall bring out the dead.' Whoever uses the light of Torah, the light of Torah will bring him back to life. Whoever does not use the light of Torah, the light of Torah will not bring him back to life.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר defends his view by giving a new source. He does not argue over the first פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר does not insist on his reading of the first פסוק. He moves to another פסוק where the 'dew' that revives the dead is 'lights', which he reads as the light of Torah. So the revival comes through Torah, and someone without Torah has nothing to revive him.

keyTerms.meaning: Expound, learn out from a פסוק
Dew of lights, read here as the light of Torah

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִקְרָא אַחֵר אֲנִי דּוֹרֵשׁ,
phrases.english: He said to him: I expound a different verse,
as it is written: "For Your dew is a dew of lights,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 26:19

phrases.english: and the earth shall bring out the dead."
Anyone who makes use of the light of Torah,
the light of Torah brings him back to life;
and anyone who does not make use of the light of Torah,
the light of Torah does not bring him back to life.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִקְרָא אַחֵר אֲנִי דּוֹרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יוחנן's objection by switching to a new source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a new source instead of defending the old reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יוחנן read 'רפאים בל יקומו' as being about one who gives himself over to עבודה זרה, it seemed that רבי אלעזר had no source for excluding עמי הארץ from תחיית המתים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק 'dew of lights' shows that revival comes through the light of Torah, so someone without Torah is not revived by it.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר offers a remedy: 'you who cleave to ה׳ are alive'
steps.stepSummary: Seeing that רבי יוחנן is upset, רבי אלעזר says he has found a remedy for the עמי הארץ in the Torah. The פסוק says that those who cleave to ה׳ are all alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he saw that he was upset, he said to him: My teacher, I have found a remedy for them in the Torah: 'But you who cleave to ה׳ your God are alive, all of you, this day.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר softens his position and brings a פסוק that offers hope to the unlearned. This step sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is that life, including life at תחיית המתים, can come from 'cleaving to ה׳', not only from learning Torah yourself. But the גמרא still has to explain how a person cleaves to ה׳, which the next steps do.

phrases.english: Once he saw that he was distressed,
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר saw that רבי יוחנן was upset.

phrases.english: he said to him: My teacher,
I have found a remedy for them from the Torah:
"But you who cleave to ה׳ your God
phrases.notes: דברים 4:4

phrases.english: are alive, all of you, this day."

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּחַזְיֵיהּ דְּקָמִצְטַעַר, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי, מָצָאתִי לָהֶן תַּקָּנָה מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending his view, רבי אלעזר offers a comforting way out for the unlearned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a Torah remedy for עמי הארץ: those who cleave to ה׳ are alive.

steps.title: Can a person really cleave to the שכינה‎? ה׳ is a consuming fire
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, still speaking, asks how a person could cleave to the שכינה, since another פסוק calls ה׳ 'a consuming fire'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is it possible to cleave to the שכינה? Doesn't it say, 'For ה׳ your God is a consuming fire'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר himself challenges the plain meaning of 'cleaving to ה׳'. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken literally, 'cleaving to ה׳' sounds impossible, because ה׳ is described as a fire that consumes everything near it. So 'cleave' must mean something else. The next step will say what it means.

phrases.english: But is it possible to cleave to the Divine Presence?
But isn't it written: "For ה׳ your God is a consuming fire"?
phrases.notes: דברים 4:24

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the literal meaning of the פסוק brought in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal reading of 'you who cleave to ה׳'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ה׳ is a consuming fire, so physically cleaving to Him is impossible. The פסוק must mean something else.

steps.title: Supporting תלמידי חכמים counts as cleaving to the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains three ways to 'cleave' to the שכינה: marrying your daughter to a תלמיד חכם, doing business for תלמידי חכמים, and benefiting them from your property. The פסוק treats such a person as if he cleaves to the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: anyone who marries his daughter to a תלמיד חכם, or does business for תלמידי חכמים, or gives תלמידי חכמים benefit from his property, the פסוק considers him as if he cleaves to the שכינה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers his own question by explaining what 'cleaving to ה׳' really means. This is the remedy for the unlearned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a person cannot literally attach himself to ה׳, he attaches himself to the people who carry the Torah. Through them he gains a share in the 'light of Torah' that revives the dead. This answers רבי יוחנן's worry for the עמי הארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: One who marries off his daughter
The פסוק considers him / credits him

steps.whatToRemember: An unlearned person can still 'cleave to the שכינה' and earn life through his connection to תלמידי חכמים: marrying his daughter to one, doing business for them, or supporting them from his property.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the harsh statement that עמי הארץ do not rise at תחיית המתים into an open door. Anyone who supports Torah has a share in its light.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: כׇּל הַמַּשִּׂיא בִּתּוֹ לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם,
phrases.english: Rather: anyone who marries off his daughter to a Torah scholar,
and one who does business for Torah scholars,
and one who lets Torah scholars benefit from his property,
the verse considers him
as if he cleaves to the Divine Presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כׇּל הַמַּשִּׂיא בִּתּוֹ לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10 by reinterpreting 'cleaving'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Cleaving to ה׳' sounded like a literal attachment, which is impossible.
steps.terutzMaskana: Cleaving means attaching oneself to תלמידי חכמים through marriage, business, or financial support, which the פסוק counts as cleaving to the שכינה.

steps.title: A second פסוק about cleaving is read the same way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a similar פסוק: 'To love ה׳ your God and to cleave to Him'. It asks the same question and gives the same answer about supporting תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the same way you say: 'To love ה׳ your God and to cleave to Him.' But can a person cleave to the שכינה? Rather: anyone who marries his daughter to a תלמיד חכם, or does business for תלמידי חכמים, or gives תלמידי חכמים benefit from his property, the פסוק considers him as if he cleaves to the שכינה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the same idea works for another פסוק that commands cleaving to ה׳. This strengthens the teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording repeats Steps 10–11 almost word for word, but now it is about a different פסוק. This shows the idea is a general rule for any mention of cleaving to ה׳, not a one-time reading. Here it even appears as a מצוה instruction, 'to cleave to Him', and not only as a promise.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not just a copy of the earlier lines. The גמרא repeats the same explanation on purpose to apply it to a second פסוק, which shows it is a general rule.

phrases.english: In a similar way you say:
"To love ה׳ your God and to cleave to Him."
phrases.notes: דברים 30:20

phrases.english: But is it possible for a person to cleave to the Divine Presence?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: כׇּל הַמַּשִּׂיא בִּתּוֹ לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם,
phrases.english: Rather: anyone who marries off his daughter to a Torah scholar,
and one who does business for Torah scholars,
and one who lets Torah scholars benefit from his property,
the verse considers him
as if he cleaves to the Divine Presence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same reading from Steps 10–11 to a second פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The teaching that supporting תלמידי חכמים counts as cleaving to the שכינה
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 30:20, 'To love ה׳ your God and to cleave to Him', read the same way

steps.title: The righteous will rise up in Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף says that in the future צדיקים will sprout up in ירושלים. He proves it from a פסוק about blossoming 'from the city', and shows that 'city' means ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף said: In the future the צדיקים will burst out and rise up in ירושלים. The פסוק says: 'They will blossom out of the city like the grass of the earth.' 'City' here means ירושלים, because another פסוק says: 'For I will defend this city.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רבי חייא בר יוסף: at תחיית המתים, צדיקים will come up out of the ground in ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof has two parts. The first פסוק says people will blossom 'from the city' like grass. The second פסוק uses 'this city' for ירושלים, so the 'city' in the first פסוק must also be ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: In the future (they are destined to)
Bursting or peeking out, like a plant breaking through the soil

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef said:
In the future the righteous will burst forth and rise up in Jerusalem,
as it says: "And they will blossom out of the city like the grass of the earth,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 72:16

phrases.english: and "city" means nothing but Jerusalem,
as it says: "For I will defend this city."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 19:34. In that פסוק, 'this city' is clearly ירושלים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement about תחיית המתים after the discussion of cleaving to the שכינה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדיקים will rise up at תחיית המתים in ירושלים, learned from 'ויציצו מעיר' together with 'העיר הזאת'.

steps.title: The righteous will rise in their clothes
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף says צדיקים will rise fully dressed. He learns it with a קל וחומר from a wheat seed, which goes into the ground bare and comes up wrapped in layers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף also said: In the future the צדיקים will stand up in their clothes. We learn this with a קל וחומר from wheat. A wheat seed is buried bare and comes up wrapped in several layers. The צדיקים are buried dressed, so all the more so they will come up dressed.
steps.whatsHappening: A second statement from רבי חייא בר יוסף: when צדיקים are revived, they will come up wearing clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a קל וחומר, an argument from a weaker case to a stronger one. A seed goes in with nothing and still comes out covered. People who went in already dressed should certainly come out dressed.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stronger case

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef said:
In the future the righteous will stand up in their clothes,
learned with a קל וחומר from wheat:
just as wheat, which is buried bare,
comes out in several layers of clothing,
phrases.notes: He means the stalk, husks and chaff that wrap around the grain.

phrases.english: then the righteous, who are buried in their clothes,
all the more so (will come out dressed).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement from the same אמורא about תחיית המתים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדיקים will rise fully clothed, learned through a קל וחומר from wheat.

steps.title: The land will grow cakes and fine wool clothing
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף says that in the future ארץ ישראל will produce ready-made cakes and fine wool garments, based on 'יהי פסת בר בארץ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף also said: In the future ארץ ישראל will produce fine cakes and fine wool clothing, as the פסוק says: 'Let there be abundant grain in the land.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third statement from רבי חייא בר יוסף: ארץ ישראל will grow finished food and clothing straight from the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the פסוק 'פסת בר' in two ways. 'בר' (grain) points to bread or cakes. 'פסת' sounds like 'פסים', fine clothing, so it points to garments.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef said:
In the future the Land of Israel will produce
fine cakes and fine wool clothing,
as it says: "Let there be abundant grain in the land."
phrases.notes: תהלים 72:16. 'פסת' sounds like 'פסים' (fine clothing, like יוסף's כתנת פסים), and 'בר' is grain for bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third statement from the same אמורא. It moves from the צדיקים to the future produce of the land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ארץ ישראל will produce cakes and fine wool clothing, learned from 'פסת בר'.

steps.title: Wheat will grow as tall as a palm tree
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the same פסוק, including its ending 'on the top of the mountains': wheat will grow tall like a palm tree and reach the mountaintops.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'Let there be abundant grain in the land, on the top of the mountains.' They said: In the future wheat will grow tall like a palm tree and rise up to the top of the mountains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the same פסוק differently: wheat will grow enormously tall. This also sets up the question that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the stress is on the words 'בראש הרים', on the top of the mountains. The ברייתא reads them to mean the wheat itself will be as tall as a palm and reach mountain height.

keyTerms.meaning: Will rise up tall, like a palm

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Let there be abundant grain in the land on the top of the mountains,"
they said: In the future wheat will grow tall like a palm tree,
and will rise up to the top of the mountains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the same פסוק that רבי חייא בר יוסף just used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future, wheat will grow as tall as a palm tree and reach the mountaintops.

steps.title: Wouldn't such tall wheat be hard to harvest?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a worry: if wheat grows that tall, harvesting it would be a real hardship.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in case you say: it will be a hardship to harvest it!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a problem with its own picture. Wheat as tall as a mountain would be very hard to cut down. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The promise was supposed to be a blessing. If the giant wheat makes the farmer's work harder, it would not feel like one, so the ברייתא has to explain how the harvest will work.

keyTerms.meaning: And in case you might say

phrases.english: And in case you say: it will be a hardship to harvest it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the picture of palm-tall wheat in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that wheat will grow as tall as a palm tree.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wheat that tall would be very hard to harvest, which would make the blessing a burden.

steps.title: A wind will bring down the flour
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the next part of the פסוק: הקדוש ברוך הוא will send a wind that knocks the flour down. A person only needs to gather a handful, and it will feed his whole household.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'Its fruit will rustle like the Lebanon.' הקדוש ברוך הוא will bring a wind from His storehouses and blow it on the wheat, and it will shake the flour loose. A person will go out to the field and bring back a handful, and from that will come his living and the living of his whole household.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the worry. Nobody will need to climb up and cut the wheat, because a wind from ה׳ will shake the flour down to the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ירעש' (rustle) points to a wind shaking the stalks. The word 'פסת' is now read as the palm of the hand, meaning one handful of flour will be enough. So the giant wheat is easy to harvest and also hugely productive.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (introduces the source for the answer)
Livelihood, what a person lives on

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חייא בר יוסף and the ברייתא both describe the future as a time of easy plenty. צדיקים rise in ירושלים fully dressed, the land grows cakes and clothing, and giant wheat drops its flour with a wind from ה׳, so one handful supports a whole family.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "Its fruit will rustle like the Lebanon":
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, תהלים 72:16. 'Rustle' hints at a wind shaking the stalks.

phrases.aramaic: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מֵבִיא רוּחַ מִבֵּית גְּנָזָיו
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, brings a wind from His storehouses
and blows it on the wheat, and makes its flour fall off,
and a person goes out to the field
and brings back a full palm of his hand,
phrases.notes: Here 'פסת' from the פסוק is read as the palm of the hand.

phrases.english: and from it comes his livelihood and the livelihood of his household.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry about how hard it would be to harvest the tall wheat.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A further reading of the same פסוק removes the problem.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Palm-tall wheat would be a burden to reap.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wind from ה׳ knocks the flour down, so gathering one handful is easy and supports the whole household.

steps.title: Wheat kernels as big as an ox's kidneys
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים explain 'עם חלב כליות חטה': in the future each wheat kernel will be as big as the two kidneys of a large ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'With the kidney-fat of wheat.' They said: In the future wheat will be like the two kidneys of a big ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new פסוק and reads it as a picture of future wheat: each kernel will be as big as an ox's two kidneys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins the word 'kidneys' with 'wheat.' The חכמים read this literally as a size comparison. The kernels will be huge, not just plentiful.

phrases.english: "With the kidney-fat of wheat"
phrases.notes: דברים 32:14

phrases.english: They said: In the future, wheat will be
like the two kidneys of the large ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of future wheat in ארץ ישראל with a new פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the future, each wheat kernel will be as big as two ox kidneys.

steps.title: Don't be surprised: the giant turnip
steps.stepSummary: To show such huge produce is believable, the גמרא tells of a turnip so big that a fox nested in it, and it still weighed sixty ליטרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't be amazed, because a fox once made its nest in a turnip. They weighed the turnip and it was sixty litra, by the litra of צפורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the giant-wheat claim with a real event from ארץ ישראל: a huge turnip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A learner might find giant kernels too hard to believe. The גמרא answers that even now the land has grown produce big enough for a fox to live inside. So giant wheat in the future is not far-fetched.

phrases.english: And do not be surprised,
for a fox once nested inside a turnip,
and they weighed it, and found it to be sixty litra,
by the litra of Tzippori.
phrases.notes: He means they used the weight standard of the town צפורי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 19 by showing that giant produce already exists.
steps.raayaObject: That wheat kernels the size of ox kidneys is believable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A real story of a turnip big enough to hold a fox's nest, weighing sixty litra.

steps.title: The giant mustard plant in שיחין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from רב יוסי: in שיחין, one broken mustard branch held nine קבין of mustard, and its wood was used to roof a craftsmen's booth.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רב יוסי said: There was a story in שיחין about a man whose father left him three mustard branches. One broke, and nine קבין of mustard were found on it. Its wood was used to roof a craftsmen's booth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another real story of huge produce, this time a mustard plant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mustard is normally a small plant. Here a single branch gave nine קבין of seeds and enough wood to roof a booth. This is more proof that the land can grow amazing produce.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rav Yosei said:
There was an incident in Shichin
involving a man whose father left him
three branches of mustard,
and one of them broke off,
and nine kav of mustard were found on it.
And its wood: they roofed a craftsmen's booth with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵי: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּשִׁיחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second story of huge produce after the turnip.
steps.raayaObject: That ארץ ישראל can grow amazingly large produce.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא story about a mustard branch with nine קבין of seed and wood big enough for roofing.

steps.title: The cabbage stalk climbed with a ladder
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן תחליפא says his father left them a cabbage stalk so tall they climbed it with a ladder.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן תחליפא said: Our father left us a cabbage stalk, and we used to go up and down it on a ladder.
steps.whatsHappening: A third story of giant produce: a cabbage stalk so tall it needed a ladder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a personal, first-hand report from a חכם. It closes the set of three stories that make giant future wheat easier to believe.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא backs up the giant future wheat of 'עם חלב כליות חטה' with three real stories of huge produce: a turnip, mustard, and cabbage.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Tachlifa said:

phrases.aramaic: קֶלַח שֶׁל כְּרוּב הִנִּיחַ לָנוּ אַבָּא,
phrases.english: Father left us a cabbage stalk,
and we would go up and down on it with a ladder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third supporting story, closing the wheat section.
steps.raayaObject: That huge produce in ארץ ישראל is realistic.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A first-hand report of a cabbage stalk climbed with a ladder.

steps.title: One grape fills a wagon in the World to Come
steps.stepSummary: Explaining 'ודם ענב תשתה חמר': in עולם הבא there is no hard work harvesting grapes. One grape is brought in a wagon, gives a large jug of wine, and its wood is used for cooking fires.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And from the blood of the grape you drank foaming wine.' They said: עולם הבא is not like this world. In this world it is hard work to pick and press grapes. In עולם הבא a person brings one grape in a wagon or on a boat, puts it in the corner of his house, and draws from it like a large jug. And its wood is burned under the cooking pot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next part of the same פסוק, now about grapes. It contrasts the hard work of grapes in this world with the easy plenty of עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this world, making wine takes picking and treading. In עולם הבא a single grape is so big it fills a wagon and can be tapped like a barrel. Even its stem gives firewood.

keyTerms.meaning: To harvest grapes and to tread (press) them

phrases.english: "And from the blood of the grape you drank foaming wine"
phrases.notes: דברים 32:14, the same פסוק as the wheat.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ: לֹא כָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: They said: The World to Come is not like this world.
In this world there is hardship
in picking and in pressing grapes;
in the World to Come, one brings a single grape
in a wagon or on a boat,
and sets it down in a corner of his house,
and draws from it as from a large jug.
And its wood: they burn it under the cooked dish.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדַם עֵנָב תִּשְׁתֶּה חָמֶר, אָמְרוּ: לֹא כָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wheat part of the פסוק to the grape part.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In עולם הבא, a single grape will fill a wagon and give a barrel of wine with no hard labor.

steps.title: Every grape gives thirty jugs of wine
steps.stepSummary: Every grape will hold thirty jugs of wine. This is learned by reading the פסוק's word 'חמר' as 'חומר', a large measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there is no grape that does not have thirty jugs of wine in it, as it says: 'And from the blood of the grape you drank foaming wine.' Do not read 'חמר' but 'חומר'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives an exact amount for each grape, thirty jugs, and shows where it comes from in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is an 'אל תקרי' reading: the same letters are read with different vowels. 'חמר' (foaming wine) becomes 'חומר', a measure of thirty סאה. That matches thirty jugs.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read (it this way, but rather...)
A large measure, equal to thirty סְאָה

steps.confusionAlert: 'אל תקרי' does not mean the פסוק's text is changed. It adds a second meaning by reading the same letters with different vowels.

phrases.english: And there is no single grape
that does not contain thirty jugs of wine,
as it is stated: "And from the blood of the grape you drank foaming wine [chamer]."
Do not read "chamer" but "chomer."
phrases.notes: A חומר holds thirty סאה, which is where the 'thirty jugs' comes from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a precise amount to the grape description and gives its source in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each future grape holds thirty jugs of wine, learned from reading 'חמר' as 'חומר'.

steps.title: Each vine needs a donkey to carry its harvest
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי explains 'אוסרי לגפן עירה': every vine in ארץ ישראל will have so much fruit that it needs a whole young donkey to carry the harvest.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: What does 'Binding his foal to the vine' mean? There is no vine in ארץ ישראל that won't need a young donkey to carry its harvest.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי brings a new פסוק from יעקב's ברכה to יהודה and reads it as a picture of the future vines of ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק pictures a donkey tied to a vine. רב דימי explains why it is there: each single vine gives so much fruit that it needs its own donkey to carry the load.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
What is meant by what is written

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
What is meant by what is written: "Binding his foal to the vine"?
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:11

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ כׇּל גֶּפֶן וָגֶפֶן שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: There is no single vine in Eretz Yisrael
that will not need one young donkey for its harvest.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new speaker and a new פסוק on the same theme of future grapes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every vine in ארץ ישראל will need a donkey to carry its harvest.

steps.title: Even fruitless trees will carry two donkey-loads
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי explains the second half of the פסוק: even trees that bear no fruit today will produce enough to load two donkeys.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And his donkey's colt to the choice vine.' There is no fruitless tree in ארץ ישראל that won't produce a load for two donkeys.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי continues with the next words of the same פסוק and goes further: even trees that bear no fruit will become fruitful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'שורקה' sounds like 'סרק', a fruitless tree. So רב דימי reads it as a tree that bears nothing today. In the future it will give enough to load two donkeys.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree that bears no fruit

phrases.english: "And his donkey's colt to the choice vine"

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָךְ כׇּל אִילַן סְרָק שֶׁבְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: There is no fruitless tree in Eretz Yisrael
phrases.notes: שורקה sounds like סרק, a tree with no fruit. That's the wordplay here.

phrases.english: that will not produce a load for two donkeys.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב דימי's reading of the same פסוק with its second half.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even fruitless trees in ארץ ישראל will produce two donkey-loads of fruit.

steps.title: This fruit will really give wine
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think this fruit has no wine. The פסוק 'כבס ביין לבושו' shows there will be enough wine to wash clothes in.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in case you say it has no wine, the פסוק says: 'He washes his garment in wine.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי heads off a possible doubt, that all this fruit gives no wine, and answers it from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lots of fruit is not the same as lots of wine. The words 'washes his garment in wine' show the fruit will be full of juice, so much that you could wash in it.

keyTerms.meaning: And lest you say, in case you think

phrases.english: And lest you say it has no wine,
the verse teaches: "He washes his garment in wine."
phrases.notes: Same פסוק, בראשית 49:11.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר אֵין בּוֹ יַיִן, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Heads off a possible doubt about steps 25-26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the vines and trees will be so fruitful.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Perhaps the fruit is plentiful but dry, with no wine in it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fruit might be plentiful but give no wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק shows there will be enough wine to wash clothes in.

steps.title: The wine will be red
steps.stepSummary: Someone might think the wine won't be red. The פסוק 'ודם ענב תשתה חמר' calls it 'blood of the grape', so it is red.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in case you say it is not red, the פסוק says: 'And from the blood of the grape you drank foaming wine.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי heads off a second doubt, that the wine might not be red, and answers from the פסוק in דברים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the wine 'blood of the grape' shows it will be red like blood. So the פסוק answers the doubt that the future wine might not be red.

phrases.english: And lest you say it is not red,
the verse teaches: "And from the blood of the grape you drank foaming wine."
phrases.notes: 'Blood' is the clue: wine called blood must be red.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר אֵינוֹ אָדוֹם, תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second doubt in the same pattern as step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The quality of the future wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Perhaps there is wine, but it is not the prized red kind.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wine might be lower-quality, not red.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Blood of the grape' shows the wine will be red.

steps.title: The future wine will make a person drunk
steps.stepSummary: The worry that this wine will not intoxicate is answered from the word סותה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe you will say this wine does not make a person drunk. The פסוק says 'סותה', which shows that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי continues the 'maybe you will say' pattern from steps 27 and 28. He answers the worry that the future wine will be too weak to make a person drunk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word סותה ('his garment') is read as sounding like מסית, 'stirs up.' So the פסוק hints that this wine is strong and really affects the drinker.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest you say; maybe you would think

phrases.english: And lest you say it does not intoxicate
phrases.notes: מרוה literally means 'soaks.' Here it means the wine makes a person drunk.

phrases.english: the verse teaches: 'his vesture (סותה)'.
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:11. The word סותה is read as sounding like 'stirring up,' meaning the wine makes one drunk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of possible worries about the future wine, each answered from a word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a word of the פסוק to answer a possible worry
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the future wine is weak and does not make one drunk.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word סותה shows it will intoxicate.

steps.title: The future wine will taste wonderful
steps.stepSummary: The worry that the wine has no taste is answered by reading חכלילי as 'every palate says: for me, for me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe you will say the wine has no taste. The פסוק says 'חכלילי עינים מיין.' Every palate that tastes it says: 'For me! For me!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the next worry: maybe the wine has no real flavor. It shows from the word חכלילי that everyone who tastes it will want more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rare word חכלילי is broken into parts: חך (palate) plus לי לי (for me, for me). So the פסוק itself hints that the taste is so good everyone wants it.

keyTerms.meaning: Red (in the פסוק); here read as חך + לי לי
Palate, the roof of the mouth used for tasting

phrases.english: And lest you say it has no flavor
the verse teaches: 'His eyes shall be red with wine.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:12.

phrases.english: Every palate that tastes it
says: 'For me, for me!'
phrases.notes: The word חכלילי is split into חך (palate) and לי לי (for me, for me).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next worry in the same series.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting a word of the פסוק into parts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the wine is strong but has no flavor.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone who tastes it says 'for me, for me,' so it tastes wonderful.

steps.title: The future wine will be good for old people too
steps.stepSummary: The worry that the wine is only good for the young is answered by reading לבן שנים as 'to one of years.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe you will say the wine is good for young people but not for old people. The פסוק says 'ולבן שנים מחלב.' Don't read it 'white of teeth.' Read it 'to one of years,' meaning an old person.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last worry in the list: maybe the wine is good for young people but not for old people. The גמרא rereads the פסוק to show it is good for them too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By changing the vowels from שִׁנַּיִם (teeth) to שָׁנִים (years), לבן שנים becomes 'to someone of many years.' So even an elderly person will enjoy this wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not read it as... (a way of rereading a פסוק with different vowels)
One of years; an elderly person

steps.whatToRemember: The whole series (steps 25-31) from רב דימי mainly uses the words of יעקב's ברכה to יהודה to show that the future vines will be hugely fruitful and their wine plentiful, red, strong, tasty, and good for everyone, young and old.

phrases.english: And lest you say it is good for the young
but not good for the old
the verse teaches: 'And his teeth white with milk.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 49:12.

phrases.english: Do not read it 'white of teeth'
but rather 'to one of years.'
phrases.notes: Meaning an old person, someone who has lived many years.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר לִנְעָרִים יָפֶה וְלִזְקֵנִים אֵינוֹ יָפֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final worry in the series, closing the list of the wine's qualities.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק with different vowels (אל תקרי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the wine is only suitable for young people.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is good for old people as well.

steps.title: What does the פסוק mean on a simple level?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the plain meaning of the פסוק is, apart from the rereadings above.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the simple meaning of this פסוק about?
steps.whatsHappening: After all the creative readings, the גמרא asks what the פסוק simply means. This sets up רב דימי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rereadings (like 'one of years') changed the words. Now the גמרא wants the meaning of the פסוק as it is written, especially 'red eyes from wine' and 'white teeth from milk.'

keyTerms.meaning: The simple, plain meaning of the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: This is a real question, not an attack. The rereadings stay true; the גמרא simply also wants the plain meaning.

phrases.english: The plain meaning of the verse, what is it written about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the creative readings to the simple meaning of the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The straightforward meaning of 'חכלילי עינים מיין ולבן שנים מחלב.'

steps.title: רב דימי: Israel asks הקב״ה for a loving look and a smile
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי explains that the פסוק is כנסת ישראל asking הקב״ה to show love with His eyes and His smile.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: כנסת ישראל said to הקב״ה: 'Master of the World, wink at me with Your eyes, which is sweeter than wine, and show me Your teeth in a smile, which is sweeter than milk.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers the question. The פסוק is a request from the Jewish people to הקב״ה to show them warmth and love.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מיין is read as 'more than wine' and מחלב as 'more than milk.' So a loving look from הקב״ה is sweeter than wine, and His smile is sweeter than milk.

keyTerms.meaning: The community of Israel, the Jewish people as a whole

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
The congregation of Israel said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the World,
wink [to me] with Your eyes
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: which is sweeter than wine,
and show me Your teeth
phrases.notes: He means smile at me.

phrases.english: which is sweeter than milk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the simple meaning of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק is כנסת ישראל asking הקב״ה for a loving look sweeter than wine and a smile sweeter than milk.

steps.title: This supports רבי יוחנן: a smile is better than milk
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי's reading supports רבי יוחנן, who taught that smiling at a friend is better than giving him milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן said: One who shows his white teeth to his friend in a smile is better than one who gives him milk to drink. As it says 'ולבן שנים מחלב.' Don't read 'white of teeth,' but 'whitening of teeth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב דימי's explanation backs up a teaching of רבי יוחנן about how valuable a smile is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both say a smile is 'more than milk.' רבי יוחנן rereads לבן as ליבון, the act of showing white teeth, and turns it into a lesson for everyone: a warm smile gives a friend more than a drink of milk.

keyTerms.meaning: One who whitens teeth, meaning one who smiles

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical lesson in בין אדם לחבירו: a warm smile is a real gift to another person.

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Yochanan,
for Rabbi Yochanan said:
Better is one who whitens his teeth to his friend
phrases.notes: He means showing your teeth in a smile.

phrases.english: than one who gives him milk to drink,
as it says: 'And his teeth white with milk.'
Do not read it 'white of teeth'
but rather 'whitening of teeth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב דימי's explanation fits with an earlier teaching of רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's teaching that smiling at a friend is better than giving him milk
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב דימי's reading that הקב״ה's smile is 'sweeter than milk'

steps.title: ריש לקיש's teacher comes back three days late
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins: רב חייא בר אדא, the children's teacher, was gone three days, and ריש לקיש asks why.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אדא was the children's teacher of ריש לקיש. He was away for three days and didn't come. When he came, ריש לקיש asked him: 'Why were you delayed?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new story about the blessing of ארץ ישראל. This step only sets the scene and asks the question; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled here yet. The story is set up with a question from ריש לקיש, and his teacher's answer will connect back to the theme of the land's amazing produce.

phrases.english: Rav Chiya bar Adda
was the children's teacher of Reish Lakish.
He was absent for three days
and did not come.
When he came, he said to him:
phrases.notes: It is ריש לקיש asking his teacher.

phrases.english: Why were you delayed?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַדָּא מַקְרֵי דַרְדְּקֵי דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story continuing the theme of the blessings of ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet; sets up the story with ריש לקיש's question to his late teacher.

steps.title: The vine that kept producing smaller amounts each day
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אדא tells ריש לקיש that he was away harvesting a single vine his father left him. Each day it gave three hundred clusters, but the wine per cluster went down from day to day.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My father left me one vine. On the first day I picked three hundred clusters from it, and each cluster filled a jug. On the second day I picked three hundred clusters, and every two clusters filled a jug. On the third day I picked three hundred clusters, and every three clusters filled a jug. And I gave away more than half of it as ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אדא answers ריש לקיש's question from the last step and explains where he was for three days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number of clusters stays the same every day (300), but the wine shrinks: one cluster per jug, then two, then three. This pattern sets up ריש לקיש's comment in the next step about why it shrank. The story also shows how rich the land's produce was, since one vine gave hundreds of jugs.

keyTerms.meaning: A grapevine trained to climb up a tree or trellis
A large jug or jar, here filled with wine
I declared it ownerless, so anyone could take it

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב חייא בר אדא answering ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: Father left me one vine
and I harvested from it on the first day
three hundred clusters
a cluster to a jug,
phrases.notes: Each single cluster gave enough wine to fill a whole jug.

phrases.english: on the second day I harvested
three hundred clusters
two clusters to a jug,
on the third day I harvested from it
three hundred clusters
three clusters to a jug,
and I declared more than half of it ownerless.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דָּלִית אַחַת הִנִּיחַ לִי אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's question about why רב חייא בר אדא was absent for three days.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב חייא בר אדא missed three days of teaching
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He was harvesting a huge yield from one vine his father left him, which gave less wine each day.

steps.title: Missing the children's learning cost him wine
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש tells רב חייא בר אדא that if he had not stayed away from teaching, the vine would have produced even more.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If you had not stayed away, it would have produced more.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש closes the story by explaining why the harvest shrank each day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The drop from one cluster per jug to three clusters per jug is not random. ריש לקיש links it to the children's Torah learning that was stopped while their teacher was away. The blessing in the land depended on the learning continuing.

keyTerms.meaning: You stayed away, you stopped your work (here, teaching)
If not, had it not been that

steps.whatToRemember: The vine's blessing kept shrinking while the children's learning was stopped; Torah learning keeps the blessing going.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Now ריש לקיש is talking.

phrases.english: If you had not stayed away
phrases.notes: He means staying away from teaching the children, which stopped their learning.

phrases.english: it would have produced more.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי לָאו דְּאִיפַּגַּרְתְּ הֲוָה עָבְדָא טְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב חייא בר אדא's report and explains the shrinking yield.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Stopping children's Torah learning lessened the blessing of the harvest.

steps.title: Goats and figs in בני ברק: milk and honey mixing
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר יחזקאל sees goats under fig trees in בני ברק, with honey dripping from the figs and milk from the goats, mixing together. He says this is 'flowing with milk and honey.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר יחזקאל came to בני ברק. He saw goats eating under fig trees, honey dripping from the figs and milk dripping from the goats, and the two mixing together. He said: This is what 'flowing with milk and honey' means.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins, showing in a very literal way how ארץ ישראל flows with milk and honey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So much honey drips from the figs and so much milk from the goats that the two actually mix on the ground. רמי בר יחזקאל uses this sight to explain the פסוק's words literally. This opens a chain of eyewitness reports about the land's richness.

keyTerms.meaning: Happened to come to a place
Flowing with milk and honey, the Torah's praise of ארץ ישראל

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל אִיקְּלַע לִבְנֵי בְרַק,
phrases.english: Rami bar Yechezkel happened to come to Bnei Brak,
he saw those goats
that were eating beneath fig trees
and honey was dripping from the figs
and milk was dripping from them
phrases.notes: "Them" means the goats.

phrases.english: and it was mixing together.
He said: This is "flowing with milk and honey."
phrases.notes: שמות 3:8

steps.triggerLanguage: רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל אִיקְּלַע לִבְנֵי בְרַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new series of stories about the fertility of ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The phrase 'flowing with milk and honey' was literally seen in בני ברק.

steps.title: Walking ankle-deep in fig honey from לוד to אונו
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב בן דוסתאי reports that once, walking early in the morning the three מיל from לוד to אונו, he walked up to his ankles in honey from figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בן דוסתאי said: From לוד to אונו is three מיל. Once I set out early at dawn, and I walked up to my ankles in fig honey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second eyewitness report about how much honey the land produced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the fig honey is not just dripping; it covers the road deep enough to reach a person's ankles. He gives the exact distance to show the whole stretch of road was like this.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of distance, about one kilometer
I set out early, at dawn

phrases.english: Rabbi Yaakov ben Dostai said:
From Lod to Ono is three mil,
once I set out early at dawn
and I walked up to my ankles
in honey of figs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי: מִלּוֹד לְאוֹנוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה מִילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another eyewitness report of the land's honey.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The road from לוד to אונו was ankle-deep in fig honey.

steps.title: ריש לקיש saw a huge milk-and-honey area by צפורי
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says he himself saw the 'flowing with milk and honey' of צפורי, an area sixteen מיל by sixteen מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: I myself saw the 'flowing with milk and honey' of צפורי, and it was sixteen מיל by sixteen מיל.
steps.whatsHappening: A third eyewitness, ריש לקיש, reports a much bigger area flowing with milk and honey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reports are growing in size: from one spot in בני ברק, to a three-מיל road, to an area sixteen מיל on each side. ריש לקיש stresses he saw it with his own eyes.

keyTerms.meaning: A major city in the גליל

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
I myself saw
the "flowing with milk and honey" of Tzippori,
and it was sixteen mil by sixteen mil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: לְדִידִי חֲזֵי לִי ״זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבָשׁ״ שֶׁל צִפּוֹרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the previous reports with a much larger area.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The milk-and-honey area of צפורי measured sixteen by sixteen מיל.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה saw the milk and honey of all ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה begins to report that he himself saw the 'flowing with milk and honey' of all of ארץ ישראל. His statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: I myself saw the 'flowing with milk and honey' of all of ארץ ישראל,
steps.whatsHappening: The biggest report of all begins: רבה בר בר חנה says he saw the milk and honey of the whole land. The גמרא is setting up the details, which come right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chain of reports reaches its widest point: not one city's area but all of ארץ ישראל. The sentence is not finished here, so the measurement he gives comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: All of the Land of Israel

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said:
I myself saw

phrases.aramaic: ״זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבָשׁ״ שֶׁל כׇּל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: the "flowing with milk and honey" of all of Eretz Yisrael,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: לְדִידִי חֲזֵי לִי ״זָבַת חָלָב וּדְבָשׁ״ שֶׁל כׇּל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the eyewitness chain from צפורי to the entire land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה בר בר חנה saw the milk-and-honey area of all ארץ ישראל (details follow).
